At every age, the spread runs the full height of the chart.
At every age, the spread runs the full height of the chart.
That vertical spread is what the screen is reading. It is not the project kind — the colours are mixed at every height — and
it is not portfolio size, which correlates with the certification rate at only r=+0.26. Median project AGE is the real
confound at r=+0.54, which is why it is on the horizontal axis and why every score in this repo is matched on it. What is left
after age is the developer, and it is worth more than the project type and the age put together. Estimated annual credits are
drawn nowhere here: against the certification rate they sit at r=-0.02.
Gold Standard registry, captured 2026-09-22; developers with at least five projects listed on or after 2020. Unlike the screening
plate, the rates here are PLAIN PORTFOLIO RATES and include the developer's own projects — this plate describes the spread that
exists, it does not score anything, and nothing downstream reads it. The leave-one-out scores are built in certification_model.py and
used only there. A developer at exactly 0% or exactly 100% with five projects is a small sample, which is why the mark carries the
portfolio size and why 24 on the floor is reported as a count rather than a rate.
